questions.prompt: 9-handed, 100bb, folded to under the gun. What do you do with 22?

choices.text: Open and call a 3-bet for set value

questions.explanation: A small pair under the gun is dominated by the opens behind and plays poorly at 100bb from first position.

questions.prompt: Same seat, folded to you, with QQ. What is the clear mistake?

choices.text: Limping so you can trap the blinds
Opening and folding to a large 4-bet from a tight player

questions.explanation: Limping queens gives the table a cheap flop and invites multiway pots. Open them.

questions.prompt: Middle position, folded to you, 100bb. Which hand moves from a UTG fold to an open?
questions.explanation: AJo is too dominated for a tight UTG open and becomes a reasonable middle-position open.

questions.prompt: You are under the gun with KQs. Which plan fits a 100bb live open?

choices.text: Limp and fold to any raise
Fold because suited kings are speculative
Open to about 3–5 big blinds and continue versus a single reasonable 3-bet

questions.explanation: KQs is strong enough to open early and does not need an all-in or a limp.
